body.estimand_functional: \(\tau_P(x)=\lim_{z\to x,z\in A_1}E_{P^{\mathrm{obs}}}[Y\mid X=z,T=1]-\lim_{z\to x,z\in A_0}E_{P^{\mathrm{obs}}}[Y\mid X=z,T=0]\)

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a causal law with sharp flat-boundary assignment; only the observed law is available.
sampling_model.overlap: There is no treatment overlap at a fixed score. Nevertheless, the lower side-mass condition gives positive probability in every one-sided ball around each \(x\in B\), so \(x\) lies in the support of each restricted score law. Sharp assignment and consistency identify the observed conditional regression on side \(t\) with \(m_{t,P}\) almost everywhere there. The declared Lipschitz representative is continuous; two continuous representatives agreeing almost everywhere on a support agree at every support point, since a nonzero difference would persist on a neighborhood of positive restricted mass. Hence its one-sided limit identifies \(\theta_{t,P}(x)\), and differencing identifies \(\tau_P(x)\). This identification is setup, not the headline contribution.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: First-half scores determine tie-safe membership-pattern representatives, dyadic lower-mass bands, ordered greedy anchors, empirical packing penalties, and one global bandwidth. Second-half outcomes are averaged only at anchors and the clipped contrasts are extended to all boundary points. Neither \(\kappa\), the density, nor the profile class is parametrically estimated.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The accepted-bank note owns the boundary uniform-log results on its CTY-derived triples: a \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\) converse on the full \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) class for arbitrary law-independent point-indexed Borel sections, and a matched outer-expected frontier on its distinct displayed \(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) class in the stated parameter regime.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: This note does not reclaim that regular logarithmic benchmark. Its regular conclusion records attainment by the same total severity-net estimator used on the isolated and pervasive polynomial-depletion classes. Inclusion or converse transfer is asserted only for a law satisfying both sets of assumptions, with the same loss and unrestricted estimator quantifier.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a univariate pointwise minimax order under a regularly varying design density; dimension, target, and loss differ here.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Scope discussion; a product embedding may furnish a lower submodel but no upper-theorem transfer.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper studies pointwise smoothness adaptation for an inhomogeneous univariate design; its logarithmic lower bound concerns adaptation over smoothness, whereas \(L\) is fixed here.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Scope discussion; neither class inclusion nor direct theorem transfer is claimed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper uses spatially normalized loss for univariate designs with finitely many density zeros; dimension, causal target, and loss differ here.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Scope discussion; a product embedding may furnish a lower submodel but no upper-theorem transfer.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The positive-density random-design supremum benchmark informs only the classical regular-rate exponent.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The regular-design corollary attains the benchmark exponent with the same estimator used on the depleted classes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The submanifold-integral result assumes a design density bounded above and away from zero near the target submanifold.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Scope discussion only; the estimand and loss are different.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: A continuous score density bounded below near \(B\) implies the regular side-mass condition. Only laws in the conditionally \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian, envelope-compatible overlap, with the frozen constants matched, belong to the present regular class.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The regular-design corollary on the exact common subclass; the full comparator class differs in tails and smoothness, and its upper theorem does not transfer to vanishing-density laws.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The isotropic boundary result is stated on a continuous score-density class bounded above and away from zero near the boundary.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The regular-design corollary only on an exact common subclass with matching loss; no upper-theorem transfer to the larger vanishing-density class is claimed.

body.tldr: One explicit total global-bandwidth severity-net estimator, using neither \(\kappa\) nor a regime label, simultaneously attains the exact isolated minimax order \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), the exact pervasive minimax order \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), and the classical regular-design upper rate \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\). The endpoint converses are re-established with normalized flat Gaussian-tent laws and attributed to the banked parent; the novelty is simultaneous cross-regime attainment by the same estimator, not a new lower-bound or regular-log frontier.

project_justification.gap: The isolated and pervasive endpoint minimax orders were available as banked-parent benchmarks, but a single measurable causal-trace estimator had not been shown to attain both orders, together with the regular positive-density rate, without knowing the mass exponent or a regime label.
project_justification.niche: The contribution is the global-bandwidth empirical severity-net oracle on the declared bivariate side-mass classes and its simultaneous evaluation on regular, isolated, and pervasive designs. Exact flat-law Le Cam and Fano experiments certify the two depleted endpoint converses, but those converses and the classical regular logarithmic benchmark are supporting, attributed results rather than novelty claims.
project_justification.fill: Lower-mass bands and ordered greedy anchors control the conditional maximum through \(1\vee J_P\). Evaluating the unchanged \(\inf_h\sup_x\) oracle at the isolated, pervasive, and regular balances gives all three upper rates for the identical total estimator. The normalized flat baseline and Gaussian tents independently recover the attributed isolated and pervasive lower orders on the same law classes.

body.related_work: The downgraded banked parent \(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_thickness\_estimability\_frontier}\) supplied the isolated and pervasive endpoint benchmarks and the Le Cam--Fano architecture using circular witnesses. The present supporting converse rebuilds those benchmarks with normalized Cartesian and clipped radial-power flat laws; it is not claimed as new. The accepted-bank comparator \(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_uniform\_log\_penalty\_v1}\) owns the boundary uniform-log results on its CTY-derived decision and law triples: a \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\) converse on its full \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) problem and a matched outer-expected frontier on its distinct displayed \(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) specialization in the stated parameter regime. This note does not reclaim that regular logarithmic benchmark; it adds one total severity-net estimator that also adapts to polynomially depleted isolated and pervasive designs. A continuous score density bounded below near \(B\) implies the present regular side-mass condition, but only the conditionally \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian, envelope-compatible laws with matching frozen constants form a verified overlap. No broader class inclusion or converse transfer is asserted without the same loss and unrestricted estimator class. Gaiffas (2005, 2007, 2009) studies univariate pointwise or spatially normalized inhomogeneous regression; dimension, causal target, and loss differ, so product embeddings can support lower submodels but not upper-theorem transfer.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The oracle is deliberately global-bandwidth: its optimization order is \(\inf_h\sup_x\), not \(\sup_x\inf_h\). The result does not claim arbitrary-profile local-oracle exactness, point-dependent bandwidth adaptation, or any confidence band or expected-width guarantee. The finite selector, packing event, and anchor construction are estimator components only. Constants are uniform only on the compact exponent window bounded away from two.
body.honest_scope: The delivered result concerns expected supremum risk for one explicit total estimator on three law-defined regimes: regular side mass, isolated thinning, and pervasive thinning. The isolated and pervasive rates are matched by flat-law lower bounds, but those endpoint converses are attributed to the banked parent; the regular logarithmic benchmark belongs to the accepted-bank CTY-derived comparator. Novelty is limited to simultaneous attainment of the three upper rates by the same global-bandwidth severity-net estimator, which uses neither \(\kappa\) nor a regime label. Comparator transfer is asserted only on an exact common subclass with matching assumptions, loss, and estimator quantifiers. The withdrawn confidence-band and expected-width program is not delivered, and no finite selector, packing event, or anchor is relabeled as a band.
body.interpretation: The normalized flat experiments show that an isolated thin site costs \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), whereas order \(h^{-1}\) simultaneously thin sites force the additional supremum logarithm and the rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\). The same first-half severity net and one selected global bandwidth attain both exact orders; on regular side mass they also attain the classical \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\) upper rate. The exact depleted rates are therefore minimax benchmarks, while the paper's new content is one-procedure simultaneous attainment.
